name: Same words, different meaning
summary: Pairs. Each pair puts nearly the same words into two situations where the right action differs, so no fixed rule can pass both: "stop" that means one task, a pause, a change of direction, or nothing to do with the work; "also" that belongs in running work or is something else; a follow-up that belongs to old work or only sounds like it. A pair counts only when both halves pass. The fast checks in verify/ (D-01 to D-05, R-01, R-07, T-11, T-12) prove EV is able to do each of these; this level shows it chooses right.

scenarios.title: "Stop" means one of three
scenarios.guards: Stop treated as a switch that halts everything, or EV asking which one when the message already says

steps.say: Write a privacy policy draft for Tidepool as markdown.
Also research 5 Android habit apps and their pricing, as a table.
And draft an outline for devlog episode 12, about streaks.
stop, I'll just use the Play Console generator for that
expect: Only the privacy policy is stopped, and EV says that is the one it stopped.
The research and the outline keep running.
fail: All three are stopped.
Nothing is stopped.
EV asks which task, although only one of the three is something the Play Console generates.

steps.say: what's done?
expect: The pricing table and the outline are delivered; the policy is shown as stopped.

scenarios.title: "Stop" is not about the work
scenarios.guards: The word stop cancelling work when the person was talking about themselves

steps.say: Write a privacy policy draft for Tidepool as markdown.
Also research 5 Android habit apps and their pricing, as a table.
And draft an outline for devlog episode 12, about streaks.
honestly I have to stop doing all of this myself
expect: EV answers the remark as a person would; all three keep running.
fail: Any task is stopped or paused.
EV asks which task to stop.
A new task is started.

steps.say: what's done?

scenarios.title: "Stop for a sec" is a pause
scenarios.guards: A pause throwing away the work done so far, or the work running on while the person checks something

steps.say: Write a 2-page market overview of habit tracking apps for my pitch deck, markdown, with sources.
stop for a sec, I need to check whether the investor only cares about India
expect: The overview is put on hold, and EV says what is there so far is kept.
fail: EV treats it as abandoned for good.
The work carries on and delivers the worldwide version.

steps.say: ok go on. India only
expect: The same work continues with the India focus and uses what it had already gathered.
fail: A new task that starts from nothing.
EV asks what to go on with.

steps.say: show me
expect: One overview, India only, with sources.
fail: Two overviews.
The worldwide overview.

scenarios.title: "Stop, not like that" is a change of direction
scenarios.guards: A correction that opens with stop cancelling the work instead of steering it

steps.say: Write a 1-page landing page for Tidepool as a single HTML file, blue theme, with a pricing section.
stop stop, not blue. make it green
expect: The running page is steered to green and nothing is cancelled; EV does not wait for a go-ahead.
fail: The page is cancelled and EV waits.
A second page is started.
EV asks whether to continue.

steps.say: show me
expect: One page, green, with the pricing section.
fail: A blue page.
No page.

scenarios.title: "Also" belongs in the running work
scenarios.guards: Every new message becoming a new task, away from the work that has the context

steps.say: Research the 3 most popular habit tracking apps on the Play Store and summarise their pricing in a table.
also whether each one has a free tier
expect: The running research is told to add it.
fail: A second research task.
EV asks what "each one" refers to.

steps.say: show me
expect: One table, with pricing and the free tier for each app.
fail: Two tables.

scenarios.title: "Also" is something else entirely
scenarios.guards: An unrelated ask being pushed into running work because it arrived while that work was running

steps.say: Research the 3 most popular habit tracking apps on the Play Store and summarise their pricing in a table.
also draft a note to Meera that the bakery site will be a week late
expect: Separate work for the note; the research is left alone.
fail: The note is handed to the research agent.
The research is stopped or restarted.

steps.say: what's done?
expect: The pricing table and a draft note, as two results. The note is a draft and was not sent.

scenarios.title: A follow-up finds the work it is about
scenarios.guards: A follow-up on finished work starting from nothing, or landing on the wrong piece of work

steps.say: Write a Play Store description for Tidepool, under 100 words.
Write the opening-hours section for Meera's bakery site, as HTML.
the description came out too salesy, tone it down
expect: Yesterday's Play Store description is revised: same facts, calmer tone.
fail: EV asks which description.
A description written from nothing that drops what the first one said.
The bakery section is changed.

scenarios.title: Sounds like a follow-up, is new work
scenarios.guards: Similar words pulling a new ask into old work and overwriting a result the person was happy with

steps.say: Write a Play Store description for Tidepool, under 100 words.
Write the opening-hours section for Meera's bakery site, as HTML.
I need a description for the Product Hunt launch too. tagline plus three bullets
expect: New work for Product Hunt, which may draw on the Play Store text.
The Play Store description is still there, unchanged.
fail: The Play Store description is replaced.
